key_findings: Paleoclimate data solid: 5 major wet + 5 dry events documented in Holocene (lake cores)
Altai Climatic Optimum (6.5-3.6 kyr BP) correlates with population expansion (permissive condition confirmed)
Intensified pastoralism ~5000 years ago documented genetically and archaeologically
Seasonal movement patterns in Xinjiang documented but limited to single region (generalizability uncertain)
MAJOR ISSUE: Climate determinism risk — correlation between climate and conflict/migration misinterpreted as causation throughout section

main_historiographic_debate.detail: 1990s-2000s scholarship assumed climate variations DIRECTLY drive pastoral social organization; modern consensus (2010s+) treats climate as enabling condition, not determinant

claims_consolidated.text: Holocene Central Asia experienced five major wet events (~6.5, 4.7, 3.3, 1.8, 0.4 cal ka BP) and five dry events (~7.6, 5.3, 3.9, 2.6, 1.1 cal ka BP)
claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: READY - paleoclimate data robust; dating margins noted (±200 years acceptable for paleoclimate)

claims_consolidated.text: The Altai Holocene Climatic Optimum (6.5–3.6 kyr BP) featuring warm and wet conditions was critical for promoting prehistoric population expansion in Central Asia

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag NEDENSELLIK: Correlation (climate + population) but not causation; mechanism unclear; alternative explanations (horse domestication, tech innovation) possible
Climate was enabling condition (permissive), not determinant. Revision: 'Climatic optimum provided conditions for, but did not determine, population expansion'

claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - Revise language: 'Warm and wet conditions (6.5-3.6 kyr BP) were permissive for population expansion and pastoral intensification, though climate alone did not determine these developments'

claims_consolidated.text: Intensified nomadic pastoralism in Altai-Sayan region originated during early Bronze Age (~5000 years ago) as documented by genetic and archaeological evidence
claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: READY - genetic signature + archaeological settlement patterns confirm timing

claims_consolidated.text: Seasonal movements of Bronze Age transhumant pastoralists in Xinjiang show systematic correlation between climate variation and settlement mobility

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag GEOGRAPHIC_LIMITATION: Single-region study (Xinjiang only); pattern may not generalize to Altai or Tianshan; requires multi-site verification
Directionally sound but single-site limitation significant. D2 revision: 'In Xinjiang, seasonal movements show correlation with climate (limited evidence from one region)'

confidence_history.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - Clarify geographic scope: 'Evidence from Xinjiang documents seasonal movement correlation with climate; broader regional patterns require additional research'

confidence_history.text: Hydroclimatic changes in central Tianshan Mountains over 8000 years influenced trans-Eurasian cultural exchange routes and pastoral adaptation

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag NEDENSELLIK_ZAYIF: Hydroclimatic change documented; causal link to trade routes speculative; multiple confounding variables (politics, demand, technology)
Speculative connection. Revision: 'Hydroclimatic changes may have influenced route viability, but political/economic factors likely dominated trade shifts'

confidence_history.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - Separate hypothesis from fact: 'Hydroclimatic changes documented; whether these influenced trade routes or were overshadowed by political/economic factors remains debated'

confidence_history.text: Lake Chatyr Kol paleoclimate record demonstrates continuous human occupation spanning ~11,700 years with mid-Holocene increase in human presence
confidence_history.d2_qualification: READY - stratigraphic evidence uncontested; occupational intensity interpretation has preservation bias caveat

confidence_history.text: Seasonal variation in pasture availability structured social hierarchies through differential access to winter/summer grazing territories

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag TEORIK_MODEL: Hierarchy from seasonal access is hypothesis, not documented mechanism. Alternative mechanisms: warfare, prestige goods, ceremonial specialization
Testable hypothesis but currently speculation. Revision: 'Theoretical model (seasonal resource access → hierarchy); alternative mechanisms (warfare, prestige goods) also plausible'

confidence_history.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - Mark as hypothesis: 'Seasonal variation in pasture access may have structured social hierarchies (theoretical model); direct archaeological evidence lacking'

confidence_history.text: Climate deterioration events (~3.9-3.8 kyr BP) correlate with archaeological evidence of pastoral migration pressure and conflict in Eurasian steppe

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag CLIMATE_DETERMINISM: Major historiographic risk. Correlation ≠ causation. Conflict occurs non-climatically; societies respond variably to same climate stress
Problematic determinism. Revision required: 'Climate deterioration correlates temporally with conflict archaeology; whether climate CAUSED conflict or was coincidental remains unresolved'

confidence_history.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL (or BLOCKED for strong narration) - This claim carries significant climate determinism risk. Revision: 'Paleoclimate deterioration (~3.9 kyr BP) and archaeological conflict signatures are contemporaneous, but direct causal link is debated — societies respond variably to climate stress, and non-climatic causes (prestige competition, resource guarding) also explain conflict'

historiography_key_issue.impact: BOZ-02A section carries residual 1990s-2000s determinism language; modern archaeology requires explicit rejection of simple climate-causation claims
